title: Compact handshake + graceful exit PRD (draft)
content:
Context:
This is an early PRD sketch for a lightweight customer-managed-network (CMN) onboarding/exit flow that minimizes audit payload size while preserving forensic value. A recurring ask from SRE/platform buyers: make VPC handshakes and evidence bundles small, fast to transfer (sometimes over low-bandwidth customer channels), and easy to store for long-tail legal retention. Existing proposals in this folder cover heavy attestation and full evidence sets; this doc explores a compact alternative that prioritizes fast onboarding, cheap retention, and a robust graceful-exit/rollback path for customers who want minimal footprint.

Problem statement:
- Full audit bundles are large (MBs–100s of MBs) and slow to upload to customer-escrow or internal storage.
- Customers with limited egress, regulatory constraints, or short pilot windows ask for a tiny canonical "handshake packet" to prove a change/hand-off occurred without exporting full telemetry.
- Risk: overly compact evidence can be insufficient for later investigations; we need to balance compression with forensic capability.
- Current UX for rollback is manual and slow; we need a predictable, signed exit path that is easily verifiable by both customer and Redwood support.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Define a compact evidence envelope (<= 20KB typical) that proves: who initiated, time window, change summary, signed hash pointers to any external fuller artifacts, and a minimal set of integrity checks.
- Provide a graceful-exit protocol that allows automated rollback tokens + a human-escrow verification path.
- Keep onboarding latency sub-5s for handshake completion in typical conditions.
- Make the system pluggable into Private control plane (VPC) and on-prem package.
- Provide developer SDK helpers and a Console UX for quick verification and export.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not attempt to replace full attestation frameworks (HSM-backed signing, full forensic capture).
- Not proposing a new long-term retention backend; aim to be compatible with existing archive/export APIs.

High-level design:
1) Compact evidence envelope (CEE)
   - Format: JSON-LD-ish single-line blob for compactness, Base64-safe.
   - Fields (min set):
     - version (string)
     - changelist_id (string, company-generated)
     - actor (short principal id)
     - action_summary (short human readable summary, <= 256 chars)
     - timestamp_range (start_ts,end_ts)
     - short_hash_map (list of object:resource->sha256_prefix(16 bytes))
     - fallback_uris (optional list of signed URIs to full artifacts, if available)
     - signature (compact ed25519 or ECDSA DER, single string)
   - Implementation note: store sha256_prefix (128 bits) not full hash to reduce size while retaining collision resistance for practical workloads.

2) Handshake flow (onboarding)
   - Customer operator triggers onboarding via Console or CLI.
   - Redwood creates a transient changelist and pre-populates expected short_hash_map entries for the outbound pieces (routing config, firewall rules diff, operator metadata).
   - Customer agent bundles the CEE and returns a signed acceptance token.
   - Redwood returns a signed acceptance ack that includes a rollback_token valid for N days (configurable) and a pointer to longer-term evidence if present.

3) Graceful-exit / rollback design
   - Rollback token: short opaque token signed by Redwood KMS, contains changelist_id, expiry, and rollback policy id.
   - Token use: when invoked, system performs an idempotent revert action (best-effort) and emits a new CEE describing the revert.
   - Audit visibility: both customer and Redwood get the revert CEE; Console shows a single-line timeline entry for compact events with expandable full-artifact links.

4) Evidence multiplexing & retrieval
   - CEEs are intentionally tiny; they include signed URIs (S3 pre-signed or customer-provided gateway) for full traces if needed.
   - If customers cannot host full artifacts, Redwood will optionally store full artifacts in encrypted cold storage and expose a retrieval-with-approval workflow. Retrieval requests generate a retrieval_evidence CEE that records who pulled what and why.

5) Data retention & cost model
   - Default: keep CEEs for 7 years (policy-aligned), with configurable retention by enterprise customer.
   - Full artifacts: default 90 days in hot storage, then cold for up to 1 year unless customer opts for longer.
   - Pricing note: compact CEEs are billed as metadata (no storage surcharge), full artifact retrieval has data-transfer+storage costs billed to customer.

Console/UX interactions:
- Onboarding modal shows a concise "Compact handshake summary" (actor, summary, timestamp, rollback window) with a single CTA: Accept & Store.
- After acceptance, customer sees a toggled timeline: Compact events visible by default; admins can request full artifacts via the retrieval workflow (2-step approval).
- Rollback: a single-button "Trigger rollback (uses rollback token)" with a mandatory short justification (free text).

Security & compliance considerations:
- Signatures: CEEs must be signed by the operator (customer agent) and Redwood acceptance must be signed by Redwood KMS. Use standard algorithms (ed25519 prefered for compactness).
- Non-repudiation: store signature metadata in the control plane; if customer requests, provide signed verification bundle.
- Jurisdiction & data residency: fallback URIs must respect customer-region preferences; do not automatically export full artifacts across jurisdictions without explicit consent.

Operational scenarios & failure modes:
- Missing full artifact: CEE still valid; short_hash_map incomplete. Add a 'degraded' flag; retrieval workflow required if later forensic needs arise.
- Token expiry before rollback: system returns a signed denial; allow a manual escalation path (support + customer approval) that generates an emergency rollback bundle with extra forensics.
- Collision suspicion on short_hash_prefix: if collision suspected, trigger a "forensic escalation" to pull full artifacts and compute full hashes. Documented as an SRE playbook.

Open questions / decisions required:
1) Acceptable prefix length for sha256_prefix (current proposal: 128 bits). Tradeoff: size vs. collision risk. Need risk analysis from Applied ML/crypto team.
2) Rollback token lifecycle defaults (7 days? 30 days?). Product to propose sane defaults; sales to have configurable options.
3) Legal: is a CEE + signature sufficient evidence for breach investigations in target customer jurisdictions? Consult Legal.
4) UX: should we expose CEE raw blob for advanced users or always present humanized summary?
5) Integration matrix: how does this map to Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) deployments? Small changes expected for agent signing/PKI.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): proto data model + unit tests for CEE encoder/decoder, Ed25519 signing helper, sample CLI tool.
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): server handshake endpoints, rollback token issuance, Console minimal UX and timeline view.
- Phase 2 (6 weeks): retrieval workflow + cold storage integration + approval gating.
- Phase 3 (4 weeks): SRE playbooks, legal sign-off, pilot with 2 customers.

Acceptance criteria (pilot-ready):
- CEE size average <= 20KB across common onboarding flows.
- Onboarding handshake round-trip < 5s in 95th percentile for pilot infra.
- Rollback completes automatically for 90% of pilot test cases with no manual intervention.
- Audit traceability test: forensic team can reconstruct change sequence from CEEs + available full artifacts in pilot tests.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: CEEs too small to be useful -> Mitigation: require signed fallback_uris when possible and have retrieval path.
- Risk: customer distrust of short hashes -> Mitigation: allow opt-in full-hash mode and document collision risk.
- Risk: legal/regulatory rejection -> Mitigation: legal review and per-jurisdiction opt-in flags.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Get quick feedback from Legal and Applied ML on prefix-length decision (PD-5678).
- Spike for Phase 0: Diego to author CEE encoder (github:142) and post sample blobs in this doc thread.
- Product to draft Console mockups for Compact timeline and rollback flow.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider packing multiple CEEs into a signed daily digest for customers who prefer batched evidence.
- Could offer an "evidence escrow token" customers can hand to their compliance teams; token resolves to CEE list via retrieval API with consent.

References / links:
- PD-5678 (Jira): design spike for compact evidence model
- Confluence: PD-4321-compact-evidence (draft notes)
- Related folder: private-deployments/approval-sim-sample-log-corpus-and-ux-insights.json (see retrieval ideas)

---
This is intentionally a rough draft. Looking for feedback from: Legal (evidence validity), Applied ML (hash-prefix risk), SRE (rollback reliability), and Sales/SE (configurable defaults).
